name: Le Sirenuse
positioning: The Sersale family's former villa on Via Colombo in Positano, opened as a hotel in 1951 and run by co-owner Antonio Sersale
best_for: Couples and adults, since children under six are not allowed
Travelers who care about Neapolitan antiques, artisan tiles and contemporary art
Food lovers wanting Naples and Amalfi Coast cooking at La Sponda

facts.text: The Sersale family villa, Villa Giulietta, opened as a hotel called Le Sirenuse in 1951.
Antonio Sersale is the hotel's co-owner and general manager.
The hotel is on Via Colombo, the main thoroughfare in Positano.
Gennaro Russo is the executive chef of La Sponda.
La Sponda's cooking is described as a culinary love letter to Naples, Vesuvius and the Amalfi Coast.
Aldo's is a cocktail bar and seafood grill.
Don't Worry is a listening bar with a state-of-the-art sound system and an in-house DJ.
Le Sirenuse Mare is a 25-minute private boat ride from the hotel.
The gym has Technogym equipment and is open to all guests.
The hotel runs a daily program of activities, including morning stretches and guided hikes.
Bathroom amenities are by Eau d'Italie, a fragrance and body care brand born at Le Sirenuse.

highlights.text: In the evening La Sponda is lit by hundreds of suspended candles that take an hour to light.
The floor tiles were designed for the hotel and fired in the kilns of a Salerno ceramics firm.
Le Sirenuse Mare is the hotel's beach club in Nerano.
Much of the furniture and art collected by Franco Sersale is in the 17th and 18th century Neapolitan and southern Italian tradition.
The Aveda Concept Spa has a sauna, a granite steam bath and an ice room.

considerations.text: The hotel does not allow children under the age of six.
The hotel is built into the cliffside and arranged vertically, with many stairways and level changes.
There is no private garage; valet parking is offered for a daily fee.
